newsitem.title: USA: NBA-OHIO JURY FINDS BARKLEY BLAMELESS IN BARROOM BRAWL.
newsitem.headline: NBA-OHIO JURY FINDS BARKLEY BLAMELESS IN BARROOM BRAWL.

text.p: A jury supported NBA star Charles Barkley's claim of innocence Friday, ruling that a lawsuit brought by a man bloodied during a barroom scuffle with the All-Star did not have merit.

The eight-person Cuyahoga County jury deliberated a little more than five hours over two days before exonerating Barkley, who refused an offer from his accuser, a 24-year-old man from Rochester, New York, to settle the civil suit for $12,000.
"Why should I settle with him, it's my money, I earned it," a pleased Barkley said after the verdict. "It was very important to me that all eight people said I didn't do anything wrong."
An argument between Barkley and a group of men that included Jeb Tyler escalated, and police said Tyler was left with a bloodied face.
Barkley, now with the Houston Rockets, was part of the 1996 U.S. Olympic team at the time of the incident and was in Cleveland for an exhibition game prior to the Atlanta Games.
The argument began when the group of men approached a woman talking with Barkley and Olympic teammate Reggie Miller and asked if she was sleeping with either player.

Barkley, supported by testimony from a bar bouncer, said he asked Tyler and his friends to leave but Tyler swore at him and took a step forward. Barkley testified that he did not think he landed any punches, though he wished he had.
"This is the third time I've been through something like this and the third time I've been acquitted," Barkley said.
